The nbfx Windows API defines the contract between the JavaFX window system and the application host: the WindowEnvironment SPI, registered in the global Lookup by the host.
The window system (tab panes, detached windows, docking) is self-contained. The few behaviours that need application services - detached-window bars, navigator reveal, project switching, tab home resolution - are supplied through a single WindowEnvironment resolved from the Lookup, instead of static setters on the tab pane. Every method has a safe default so a host without an environment still works.
The launcher registers a WindowEnvironment that supplies the host services.
Detached editor windows get their menu and tool bars from the environment.
The navigator-reveal and project-switch shortcuts delegate to the environment.
The defaults are unit-tested. The API is under development until the MVP freeze.
A JDK is required only to compile; JavaFX is provided by the runtime.
Only com.gluonhq.netbeans.nbfx.windows is public.
The window system resolves WindowEnvironment from the global Lookup; a host registers its implementation with @ServiceProvider.
The host module registers the implementation, not this module.
